memories.content: Do not equate BLS retail-margin PPI index changes with gross margin percentage-point changes; they measure different constructs and can move in opposite directions.

BLS retail-margin PPI indices track dollar margin per unit in index points, not gross-margin percentage points; they can rise while gross margins fall, so treat them as complementary price-pressure evidence—not a direct proxy for filing-based margins.

A small operating-to-gross margin gap combined with flat/declining inventory amid revenue growth points to SG&A deleverage rather than inventory write-downs, but quarterly cadence is required to rule out intra-year build-and-liquidate cycles.

In mass-merchant retail, company-specific cost-structure shifts (freight, labor, markdowns, digital fulfillment) routinely dominate sector-wide inflation effects on gross margin, so peer-median decomposition on a consistent 10-K basis is the primary diagnostic.

learned.content: Always verify that causal claims about 'primary' drivers match the quantitative decomposition from edgar.margin_change (company_specific_pts vs peer_median_change_pts) and include all planned peers in the peer median or document exclusions.

Never present derived percentages (e.g., revenue_change_pct, cogs_change_pct) as directly queried numbers; cite the peer-median query (edgar.margin_change) for sector-wide comparisons and the decomposition query for company-specific vs sector-wide attribution.

Use quarterly financial_fact inventory for Q1-Q3 to assess intra-year build-up risk; cite edgar.margin_change for gross/operating margin changes and revenue growth; phrase inferences as 'consistent with' with medium confidence unless direct SG&A evidence exists.

Cite the actual margin_change queries for peer gross margin declines, recalculate PPI averages from raw monthly observations in lightning.metastore.causeway.retail_usl.price_index, and verify both truckload_freight and warehousing series values before asserting cost-pressure comparisons.

In mass-merchant retail, company-specific cost-structure shifts (freight, labor, markdowns, digital fulfillment) routinely dominate sector-wide inflation effects on gross margin, so peer-median decomposition on a consistent 10-K basis is the primary diagnostic.

BLS retail-margin PPI indices track dollar margin per unit in index points, not gross-margin percentage points; they can rise while gross margins fall, so treat them as complementary price-pressure evidence—not a direct proxy for filing-based margins.
Public XBRL filings for general merchandise retailers almost never expose category-level gross profit, making mix-shift quantification impossible without management disclosures or alternative data.

A small operating-to-gross margin gap combined with flat/declining inventory amid revenue growth points to SG&A deleverage rather than inventory write-downs, but quarterly cadence is required to rule out intra-year build-and-liquidate cycles.
